## Purpose

Generate 200 placebo assignments for each of three assignment mechanisms while keeping observed outcomes fixed. Save assignments and simulation metadata for the fitting scripts.



# DATA NOTES
# dt is a long unit-by-year panel.
# Required columns (assumed by downstream code): i, year, start_year, y0, n, plus covariates for hazard.
#
# start_year is observed adoption year for the real world, repeated within unit.
# start_year == Inf indicates "never treated within window".
#
# y0 handling:
# - We remove any stale y0 columns and rebuild with set_y0().
# - y0 is "observed" only pre observed assignment; post is NA by construction.
#   This implies: simulated assignments can only REMOVE training labels (never add them).
#
# conf/Lset:
# - Lset encodes which lags/features are used by learners/hazard model (e.g. shift_max=3).
# - Stored in options(xpn.conf) so functions can find it without passing everywhere.
```{r}
# Load the county-year panel, reconstruct untreated observations and choose history lags.
# Store the lag configuration in options(xpn.conf) for downstream helper functions.
dt <- readRDS("data/notpublic/compact_dt.rds") |> data.table()
dt$year |> summary()
dt$start_year |> table()

dt[, y0_25 := NULL]
dt[, y0 := NULL]
dt |> set_y0()
table(dt$year < dt$start_year, is.na(dt$y0))

conf <- list(Lset = choose_lset(dt, shift_max = 3))
options(xpn.conf = conf)
```



# SIMULATED ASSIGNMENTS / WORLD TYPES
# Goal: Generate 3 "world types" by changing the assignment hazard cpr (unit-year weights).
# Each world is defined ONLY by how A_sim is sampled; observed y0 stays fixed.
#
# World 1: "hazard" (ignorable baseline)
# - cpr = h from get_hazard(engine="xgboost") using observed history/covariates.
# - Intended to approximate assignment MAR given observed predictors.
#
# World 2: "level" (latent level confounding)
# - Fit Poisson GLMM with random intercept (1|i): y0 ~ (1|i) + offset(log(n)).
# - u_i = exp(ranef(m)$i[,1]) is a unit-level multiplicative effect (persistent over time).
# - Set cpr := u (repeated per row) so assignment depends on latent "level".
# - NOTE: u is estimated using all observed y0, which includes years beyond what would be
#   available under a simulated assignment. This is OK because u is used ONLY to simulate
#   worlds (not fed to learners), but it creates intentionally non-ignorable assignment
#   from the analyst perspective (latent ignorability: ignorable given U, not given history).
#
# World 3: "slope" (latent trend confounding)
# - Fit Poisson GLMM with random slope (year|i): y0 ~ (year|i) + offset(log(n)).
# - s_i = exp(ranef(ms)$i[,2]) is a unit-specific multiplicative trend component.
# - Set cpr := s so assignment depends on latent trend.
#
# shuffle_a():
# - Consumes dt[, cpr] as the sampling weight/hazard by year.
# - Returns an A_sim vector (unit -> simulated start year / Inf).
# - IMPORTANT: Because y0 post observed start_year is NA, simulated assignments can only
#   create additional missing labels. "Recoverable OOB" are those made missing by sim but
#   still observed under the real world (year >= A_sim AND year < A_obs).
#
# nrep = 20 is a pilot. For stable scoring, increase reps (often >> 20) because recoverable OOB
# can be small (e.g., ~10–15%), making per-rep scores noisy.
#
# Storage:
# - a_hazard/a_level/a_slope are arrays: [unit, rep] (assuming shuffle_a returns length = #units).
# - sim_a is 3D: [unit, rep, world] with world in {"hazard","level","slope"}.
# - Saved to data/simulated_assigments.rds (note spelling).
```{r}
# Estimate observed-history hazards and latent county levels/trends, then sample 200 assignments per world.
# Combine MAR, latent-level and latent-trend assignments into a county x replication x world array.
library(lme4)
m  <- glmer(y0 ~ (1 | i), data = dt, family = poisson, offset = log(n))
u  <- exp(ranef(m)$i[as.character(dt$i), 1])
ms <- glmer(y0 ~ (scale(year) | i)
  , data = dt, family = poisson, offset = log(n)
)
s  <- exp(ranef(ms)$i[as.character(dt$i), 2])
h  <- dt |> get_hazard(engine = "xgboost")

cor(u, h)
cor(u, s)
cor(s, h)


nrep <- 200
dt[, cpr := h]
set.seed(0203)
a_hazard <- replicate(nrep, dt |> shuffle_a())
dt[, cpr := u]
set.seed(0203)
a_level <- replicate(nrep, dt |> shuffle_a())
dt[, cpr := s]
set.seed(0203)
a_slope <- replicate(nrep, dt |> shuffle_a())


sim_a <- abind::abind(
  a_hazard, a_level, a_slope
  , along = 3
  , new.names = list(NULL, NULL, c("hazard", "level", "slope"))
)

dt[i %in% 1:50] |> plot_assignment_diff(a_hazard[, 1])
```


```{r}
# Package assignment arrays with seeds, model specifications and data summaries.
# Save data/simulation/simulated_assignments_with_meta.rds for downstream model fitting.
meta <- list(
  created_at = Sys.time(),
  seed = 0203,
  nrep = nrep,

  worlds = c("hazard", "level", "slope"),

  data_info = list(
    n_units = uniqueN(dt$i),
    n_obs = nrow(dt),
    years = range(dt$year),
    start_year_table = table(dt$start_year, useNA = "ifany")
  ),

  hazard_sources = list(
    hazard = "xgboost hazard from get_hazard()",
    level  = "unit random intercept from Poisson GLMM",
    slope  = "unit random slope (year) from Poisson GLMM"
  ),

  models_used = list(
    level_model = formula(m),
    slope_model = formula(ms),
    family = "poisson",
    offset = "log(n)"
  ),

  notes = c(
    "Simulated assignments only remove labels; they never add new observed y0.",
    "World 'hazard' approximates ignorable assignment given observed history.",
    "Worlds 'level' and 'slope' induce latent confounding: ignorable given latent U, not given history.",
    "Random effects estimated on full observed panel; used only for simulation, never fed to learners.",
    "Seeds reset before each world to ensure common random numbers across worlds."
  )
)

sim_out <- list(
  assignments = sim_a,
  metadata = meta
)

saveRDS(sim_out, "data/simulation/simulated_assignments_with_meta.rds")
```
